native_names: Бухарская Народная Советская Республика (Bukharskaya Narodnaya Sovetskaya Respublika)

land.text: the whole emirate: West Bukhara with Bukhara and Karshi, East Bukhara from Hisor to the West Pamir

predecessors.note: The emirate fell on 2 September 1920 (Ark destroyed); the republic was proclaimed on 8 October 1920.

land.text: West Bukhara, to the Uzbek SSR

successors.note: Uzbek SSR (no dossier): West Bukhara except the south bank of the Amu Darya.

land.text: the south bank of the Amu Darya with Chardjui, to the Turkmen SSR
East Bukhara, to the Tajik ASSR

successors.note: Tajik ASSR within the Uzbek SSR, a Tajik SSR from 1929 (DEL); no dossier.

identity.name: Bukharan People's Soviet Republic

correction.text: the former emirate's core: 'West Bukhara, including the cities of Bukhara and Karshi' and 'East Bukhara, roughly from Hisor to West Pamir'; the shape is Cliopatria's 1919 shape unchanged, extended to 1924

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's emirate row ends in 1919. BP gives 182,193 km2; the 1919 shape is about 186,000 km2 in the gazetteer (ratio 1.02), so the shape is kept for the republic's years.

region.text: the emirate: West Bukhara and East Bukhara

ledger.note: 1920: the Bukharan People's Soviet Republic is proclaimed. 'was proclaimed on 8 October 1920 under Fayzulla Xoʻjayev', five weeks after '2 September 1920, after four days of fighting, the emir's citadel (the Ark) was destroyed'.

region.text: East Bukhara, 'roughly from Hisor to West Pamir' (BP); the Khatlon and Dushanbe admin-1s are a floor

ledger.note: 1921: Basmachi forces hold East Bukhara. 'Basmachi forces operated with success in both Khiva and Bokhara for an extended period' (1920-22); Enver Pasha 'joined the movement after November 1921' and fell near Baldzhuan on 4 August 1922. The region and year are the researcher's reading; a rebel overlay, not a change of sovereignty.
1924: the republic becomes the Bukharan Socialist Soviet Republic. 'from 19 September 1924 to 27 October 1924, the Republic was known as the Bukharan Socialist Soviet Republic'.

1924: Bukhara 'voted itself out of existence' and is divided. 27 October 1924: West Bukhara to the Uzbek SSR, the south bank of the Amu Darya with Chardjui to the Turkmen SSR, East Bukhara to the Tajik ASSR; the partition was decided in April 1924 over local opposition (DEL).

wars.name: Basmachi revolt

zones.text: East Bukhara, 'roughly from Hisor to West Pamir' (BP); the Khatlon and Dushanbe admin-1s are a floor

wars.outcome: The overthrow of the emir 'sparked the Basmachi Revolt', which 'took the Red Army until 1934 to fully suppress'; no border change while the republic lasted.

certainty.note: A revolutionary republic inside the Turkestan ASSR, drawn on the emirate's old lines; East Bukhara was never fully held.

sources.title: Bukharan People's Soviet Republic
sources.note: Overthrow 2 September 1920, proclamation 8 October 1920, territory, 182,193 km2, 1924 transfers, renaming 19 September 1924, end 27 October 1924.

sources.title: National delimitation in the Soviet Union
sources.note: April 1924 decision to partition Bukhara and Khorezm over local opposition.

sources.title: Basmachi movement
sources.note: Enver Pasha and the Basmachi in Bokhara 1921-22; the revolt sparked by the emir's overthrow.

notes:
Written for batch ia-03-x from two pages (budget 1-2): BP and DEL. The BP page does not mention the March 1921 treaty with Soviet Russia or any gain or loss of land (Kerki, Shahrisabz, Gissar, Kulyab are not on it). Cliopatria's emirate row ends 1919: the shape is carried to 1924.
The three successor entries all point to the union dossier because the Uzbek SSR, Turkmen SSR and Tajik ASSR have none; a gap-filler should re-point them if such dossiers are ever written. Counterpart basmachi-movement is written in this batch.
